info.description: Bounded simulator subset of the official Amazon Relational Database Service API (2014-10-31). Every other official operation returns HTTP 501 UnknownOperationException. DB subnet groups, DB parameter groups, DB cluster parameter groups and option groups are stored configuration served over the Query protocol: no DB instance, cluster, proxy, snapshot, event subscription, network or database engine exists, and CreateDBInstance, CreateDBCluster, CreateDBSnapshot and every other official operation return UnknownOperationException with HTTP 501. Parameter and option values are not modeled: ModifyDBParameterGroup, ResetDBParameterGroup, DescribeDBParameters, the cluster equivalents, CopyDBParameterGroup, ModifyOptionGroup and DescribeOptionGroupOptions are not implemented. Default parameter, option and subnet groups are not pre-created, and parameter group families, major engine versions and subnet IDs are stored without checking that they exist. A subnet group needs 2 to 20 distinct subnet-xxxxxxxx or subnet-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx IDs and is not checked for Availability Zone coverage; it reports no VPC, Availability Zone, Outpost, status or network type. DB subnet group and DB (cluster) parameter group names are stored in lowercase as documented, "default" subnet groups are refused, and option groups accept only the documented EngineName values. Describe operations and ListTagsForResource refuse a non-empty Filters list (an empty one means no filter), Describe operations accept MaxRecords from 20 to 100 and fail with the operation's not-found fault for an unknown name, and DescribeOptionGroups refuses OptionGroupName together with EngineName or MajorEngineVersion. Tag keys are 1 to 128 and values at most 256 characters of letters, digits, spaces and _.:/=+-@, and neither may start with aws: or rds:. Tag operations on an unknown ARN fail with DBInstanceNotFound, the first not-found fault the official tag operations model. Amazon Aurora, Amazon Neptune and Amazon DocumentDB are managed through this same RDS API (Version 2014-10-31, signing name rds, rds: IAM actions, rds ARNs), and the boto3 neptune and docdb clients and the rds client with Aurora families were run against these operations. Only the configuration above is served, not the products: no Aurora, Neptune or DocumentDB cluster, instance, snapshot, global cluster or endpoint exists, so CreateDBCluster, CreateDBInstance and their Describe operations return UnknownOperationException with HTTP 501, and no SQL, Gremlin, SPARQL, openCypher or MongoDB data plane exists. The neptune client can use 13 of the 16 operations and the docdb client 10: neither model has option groups, and DocumentDB has no DB parameter groups. Parameter group families such as aurora-mysql8.0, neptune1.3 and docdb5.0 are stored without being checked. Responses omit SubnetOutpost, which the neptune and docdb models lack, and SupportedNetworkTypes, which the neptune model lacks. The RDS rules apply to every client: a non-empty Filters list is refused although those models define it, subnet group names must start with a letter although the neptune and docdb models do not say so, and tag keys and values may contain : and @, which the neptune and docdb models do not list.
